topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the stepwise model of tumor progression, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt, RTK, Ras, and PI3K pathways, drive sustained cellular proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells arrest in immature, proliferative progenitor states across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptotic cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through alterations in p53 regulation and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress response control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere maintenance and p53-mediated stress signaling control cellular senescence and immortalization, concluding the discussion on cell-intrinsic growth control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore altered energy metabolism in tumors, focusing on aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring, and epigenetic changes induced by oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which tumors recruit vasculature to overcome diffusion limits for growth.

topics.label: Metastatic cascade, dissemination, and genomic features
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanical and biological processes governing tumor invasion, circulatory dissemination, colonization efficiency, and associated genomic alterations.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarizes the overall themes of the lecture and points students toward further literature and upcoming practicals.
